title: cloud-connection, plugin-security: a marketplace upgrade that would un-make an access choice is refused until it is confirmed (#24446 U2)
body:
Part of #24446

U2 of #24446: the marketplace refusal. It works to the measurement in 6355301005 and the seat's GO in 6355317159, under claim 6355237423. U1 (the boot report) landed as `54df640b38`. The ADR-0126 dated note is a separate Tier H docs PR that the seat cuts. #24446 remains open for it.

Clause-②: yes (narrowing): a marketplace re-install that installed before is now refused `409` while it would un-make an access choice made in this system, until the same call confirms it (narrowing); the door gains the `confirmAccessUpgrade` body field and the `ACCESS_UPGRADE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` code, plugin-security gains the `security.accessUpgradeCheck` service and its exports, and the CLI gains `--confirm-access-upgrade <token>` (widening).
Metadata-protocol: none

## What changed

**`cloud-connection`: step 2c of `POST /api/v1/marketplace/install-local`.** It runs on a managed re-install over an installed package (`findConflict === 'marketplace'`), after the D5e gate and before the first write (`manifest.register`). A fresh install has no customer choice of its own to un-make, so it is never checked. The door asks the `security.accessUpgradeCheck` service as a capability question, so `cloud-connection` takes no runtime dependency on `plugin-security`.
- **Findings:** `409 ACCESS_UPGRADE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED`, and nothing is registered or written.
  - `error.details.findings` names each finding: its kind, type, name, the candidates and binding positions, the missing names, and a one-line `describe`.
  - `error.details.findingSet` is the token, and `error.details.confirmWith` is the retry.
- **The confirmation:** the same request with `confirmAccessUpgrade: <findingSet>`.
  - The token confirms exactly the findings it names. If the findings change, it no longer matches and the call is refused again with the fresh set.
  - A bare `true` confirms nothing.
  - A confirmed install records `accessUpgradeConfirmation: { findingSet, confirmedBy, confirmedAt }` in its ledger entry.
- **The check stopped** (the ledger, the catalog or the declared rules unreadable): `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, and nothing is written.
- **No check service** (no security plugin in the composition): the upgrade proceeds, and one `warn` line says no check ran.

**`plugin-security`: `access-upgrade-check.ts` (new), registered by `SecurityPlugin` as `security.accessUpgradeCheck`.** It runs U1's `collectAccessUpgradeFindings` unchanged and restates none of its rules. It runs it twice:
1. over the registry as it stands;
2. over a projection of that registry with package P's items taken from the incoming manifest:
   - the catalog entries (permission sets, positions, capabilities) with `packageId === P`;
   - the declared sharing rules;
   - P's objects and fields: the registry's field set, less what P's previous version declared, plus the incoming declaration's.

The customer's state (the ledger, the `sys_sharing_rule` rows) is never projected. The answer is the **delta**: what run 2 finds that run 1 does not, and a finding that only grew keeps its new parts only. So a finding that predates the upgrade, or that another package caused, never blocks it; U1's boot report keeps raising those. "P's previous version" is the door's ledger entry, or else the registry's own record of the package. Sources are resolved at every call.

**`spec`: one error-code ledger row**, `ACCESS_UPGRADE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` under `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, and the three generated reference pages that list it.

**`cli`: `os package install … --confirm-access-upgrade <token>`.** It sends the token. On the refusal, it prints every finding's `describe` line and the exact retry.

## Who sees it

- **Walled (`isolated`, `group`):** only the platform operator reaches step 2c. The existing ADR-0131 D12 refusal answers a tenant administrator `403` before the check runs, and shows no finding.
- **`single`:** the administrator (`manage_metadata`).

## Limits, as in U1 (accepted by the seat, 6353222762)

- A re-enablement is "suspected": nothing records which name replaced which.
- The field-deny check reads "grants the same object", not "copied from".
- "The old name carrying a clone" is carried by the switch-off half (ADR-0126 §9).
- An object that the incoming manifest adds and the registry does not yet hold is judged on its declared fields only, without the fields the registry would inject.

## Scope held

- Not `runtime/src/domains/packages.ts` (`POST /api/v1/packages` with `overwrite`). It is the seat's follow-up card, which calls this same service.
- Not cloud's own install path. If it has one, it calls this service in cloud's follow-up.
- Not `docs/adr/**`, not U1's boot report (imported read-only), and no `ORGANIZATION_OWNERSHIP_SHAPE_GENERATION` change.
- `cloud-connection` gains `@objectstack/plugin-security` as a **devDependency** only, for its door test. There is no cycle: it already reaches plugin-security through `@objectstack/runtime`.

## Tests

- **`cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-access-upgrade.test.ts`** (34). The real door runs against the real `createAccessUpgradeCheck`, over an in-memory access state with version 1 installed through the door. For each of the four types (permission set, position, sharing rule, capability):
  - `single`: the administrator gets 409 with the finding;
  - `isolated` and `group`: the operator gets 409;
  - `isolated` and `group`: a tenant administrator gets 403 from the wall, the check is not called, and no finding is shown;
  - CONTROLs under `single` and `isolated` (200).
  - Plus: the token installs and is recorded; `true` and a stale token are refused; a finding that predates the upgrade does not block it; a stopped check gives 503 and writes nothing; no check service means 200 and a warning.
- **`plugin-security/src/access-upgrade-check.test.ts`** (15). The check as `SecurityPlugin` registers it, over a real `ObjectQL` and SQL driver, for the four types with CONTROLs. It also covers a clone naming a field the upgrade removes (version 1 read from the registry), a field deny the managed set gains, the delta, the fail-closed stop, and "unbound before start".
- **`cli/test/package-install-access-upgrade.test.ts`** (3): the flag, its absence, and the refusal's rendering.
- **Ablations**, each red and then restored from the committed source:
  - disabling step 2c turns 21 door pins red;
  - refusing on the whole projected report instead of the delta turns the "predates" pin red in both suites;
  - turning off the catalog projection turns 4 of the check's pins red.

The proof readings are in the os-dev-report on #24446: CI, the dispatch gates, `check-governed-merges --branch`, R1, R4 under `isolated` and `group`, the upgrade harness and the dogfood battery.
